notes: New features: --Added dice talents: every die can now awaken a signature talent that changes how it works during fights --one talent slot per die, and swapping or unequipping is always free, so experimenting never costs you --unlock a talent with Dice Tokens, catch it as a lucky daily Shop offer, or hunt it down inside Diamond and Master chests, where the drop odds scale with the die's rarity --the rarer the die, the rarer the talent, making higher rarities a genuine chase --talents only awaken once you truly own the die and have classed it up to the level the talent demands, so your strongest dice reveal their potential first --a talent can sharpen a die's stats, retune its skills, or grant it something entirely new --Electric, Wind and Time Dice starts off with their new obtainable talents!

Dice balance: --Iron: Skill proportional damage reduced from 14% -> 12% ---Iron Dice is quite oppressive as an anti-tank option, being able to shred even low-health units fairly quickly alongside team member, so the passive proportional damage has been lowered. --Solitude: Passive proportional max HP damage reduced from 8% -> 7% ---Much like Iron, Solitude is an auto-include in every staple deck that Iron normally thrives in, and with the duo being so strong especially in bossfights, as the passive reduction wasn't much of a downside to be able to do so much damage quickly, so it has been toned down to give players a fair chance.

Bug fixes: --resolved weird jankiness that could go possibly wrong with some transformed effects --resolved an issue that caused Shield Die's shield active to last 1 less turn than intended --resolved an issue that caused multi-hit attacks to not trigger on-damaged effects multiple times (e.g. Wind's Gale Force vs. Armor's Heavy Plating) --resolved an issue that caused bosses to be locked by Lock Dice --resolved some weird targeting behaviour caused by electric chains

Security: --hardened the random generator's fallback path so reward, shop, and combat rolls are mixed and no longer directly predictable when a browser does not expose Web Crypto, and a warning is logged when this degraded mode is active

Security: --hardened local save integrity so edited or corrupted save data is rejected and reset to safe defaults --hardened multiplayer turn handling so the server's authoritative battle state is validated before it is applied --closed a case where the playtest/dev menu could ship inside a production build
Bug fixes: --fixed a crash when a save file contained a malformed dice-progress entry

Dice balance: --Fire: Damage increased from 24 -> 26 --Fire: Splash damage increased from 12 -> 13 ---A small buff to Fire's damage output to make it feel more impactful early on. --Ice: Mana charge rate reduced from 6 -> 5 ---Ice is struggling in the current meta due to its low value, so allowing it to get freezes more frequently to bolster its viability as a control option. --Sword: Health increased from 850 -> 880 ---Sword Die's HP is a little too low for a frontline damage dealer, while also being the only Dice that has no direct skills, so it has eaten enough healthy food to sustain more in battle. --Drizzle: Health reduced from 560 -> 540 ---A small HP nerf so Drizzle can be answered more often by mid-range units. --Spear: Health increased from 880 -> 900 ---Much like Sword, Spear needs just a little more to survive the frontline as a bruiser. --Discharge: Damage increased from 25 -> 28 --Discharge's skill is often hard to get value out of and is generally awkward in a lot of situations, so we're upping its basic attack damage. --Slingshot: Health reduced from 480 -> 450 ---Slingshot is still a polarising Dice that can quickly shred low-health units with ease, so it needs some added counterplay --Broken Growth: Damage increased from 28 -> 30 ---Broken Growth Die's major downside is being able to downgrade its attack count to lower its overall damage it can deal per turn, so it needs a little more love --Reverse: Damage increased from 20 -> 22 --Reverse: Health increased from 600 -> 620 ---Reverse is fun to use with a lot of creative decks, but it just lacked sufficient stats on its own, so increasing its stats so it can hold on for a bit longer --Druid: Bear Form: Health decreased from 1,500 -> 1,400 ---The Bear was quite tanky for the opponents to deal with after finishing supporting its team, so lowering that so the opponents have a better chance at mauling it down. --Transcendence: Transformed beam damage reduced from 600 -> 520 ---It never really make sense as to why the Transcendence is truly capable of sniping enemy Dice with such an incredibly powerful attack, so lowering that to a more appropriate balance point.
